Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance
Bodily Injury Unit
Claim Notes
Claim number:
C-1407
Claimant:
Maria Jimenez
Adjuster:
Chelsea Hebert
August 12, 2023
Claim reported by the claimant following a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. The claimant reports neck
and back strain and is not represented by an attorney.
August 22, 2023
Reviewed the policy in force at the time of loss. The driver is a household member of the policyholder and is listed as
a covered operator under the household arrangement.
September 14, 2023
Spoke with the claimant, who described the collision in the same way as in the first report. The claimant has no prior
cliams history on file for this vehicle.
September 25, 2023
Police report obtained. It confirms the claimant was seated in the vehicle at the time of impact and records the
rear-end sequence as described.
October 5, 2023
Statements taken from two independent witnesses. Both confirm the accident occurred as the claimant described and
that the claimant's vehicle was stopped when struck.
November 23, 2023
Photos from the scene and the other driver's statement are consistent with the claimant's account of how the collision
happened.
January 26, 2024
Inspected the claimant's vehicle. Damage is concentrated at the rear and is laregly in line with the rpeorted impact.
No earlier damage to the vehicle is known to us or noted in prior records.
February 1, 2024
Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the start of coverage. Vehicle history and prior inspection records
show no earlier loss on the rear end.
February 4, 2024
Claimant's medical records reviewed. Reported neck and back strain fits the type and force of a rear-end impact of
this kind. No earlier injury to the same body areas appears in the records obtained.
February 6, 2024
Treatment followed a typical course, with physical therapy and follow-up visits. Treatment frequency decreased
steadily as the claimant's symptoms improved.
February 13, 2024
Claimant was contacted again and gave the same account of the accident and injuries as in earlier conversations. No
changes to the reported facts were made.
February 23, 2024
File reviewed. Liability and injury information are consistent across all sources, and the claim is ready for settlement
evaluation under the policy terms.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- occurrence_support: Do independent sources (witnesses, photos, cameras, the other driver) confirm that the accident happened as described? Allowed: Confirmed, Partially corroborated, Uncorroborated, Contradicted, Suspected staged.
- damage_crash_fit: Does the vehicle damage fit the described impact? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- account_stability: Did the claimant's account of the accident stay the same over time? Allowed: Stable, Clarified, Materially changed.
- occupant_presence: Was the claimant really in the vehicle at the time of the crash? Allowed: Verified, Unclear, Added later, Not present.
- prior_damage_evidence: Is there evidence of vehicle damage from before this crash? Allowed: None, Possible, Documented, Material.
- known_loss_evidence: Is there evidence the damage existed or was known before the coverage started? Allowed: Weak, Moderate, Strong.
- driver_status: Is the driver of the insured vehicle on the policy? Allowed: Listed, Household, Unlisted, Excluded.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
